rounds.text: Propshop Events and Exhibitions Ltd is exceptionally undervalued, trading at a modest P/E ratio of 10.6 [E1] despite exhibiting phenomenal operational profitability, highlighted by an extraordinary ROE of 52.3% and an ROCE of 71.5% [E10, E9]. This superior financial performance thoroughly dominates sector medians, with the company's ROE of 21.78% and ROCE of 29.96% vastly outstripping sector benchmarks of 5.13% and 6.66% respectively [E7, E8]. Growth metrics further validate the strong bull case, driven by a 3-year compounded sales growth of 40% alongside a staggering 102% compounded profit growth over the same period [E11, E13]. Furthermore, the business is completely debt-free with borrowings reduced to zero at Rs 0.00 Cr, supported by positive free cash flow of Rs 1.48 Cr [E24, E23]. A discounted cash flow model indicates an intrinsic value of Rs 262 per share, offering a massive margin of safety of 74.0%, while the reverse DCF implies that today's price factors in a negative growth rate of -0.7% against base expectations of 18.0% [E30, E31, E32]. Conceded: [E4] dividend yield is 0.00% and [E39] debtor days have increased from 40.2 to 56.8 days.

Despite headline profitability metrics, serious underlying risks emerge from the cash conversion and working capital dynamics of Propshop Events and Exhibitions Ltd [E21]. Cash conversion sits at a concerning 0.23x against reported profit for March 2026, indicating that reported profits are running far ahead of actual cash generation due to potential receivables or accruals issues [E21]. This disconnect is further corroborated by the expansion of debtor days, which have increased from 40.2 to 56.8 days [E39]. Furthermore, despite reporting repeated profits, the company distributes a dividend yield of 0.00%, withholding cash from shareholders [E4, E38]. Operating margins add to the operational uncertainty, showing an inconsistent yearly trend over the last two years and a minor compression in TTM down to 16% from 17% three years earlier [E18, E19]. Conceded: [E13], [E24].

Conceded: [E21], [E39], [E38]. While the bear points to rising debtor days, the company nonetheless successfully converted those operations into positive absolute cash flow, generating Rs 1.82 Cr in operating cash flow and Rs 1.48 Cr in free cash flow for March 2026 [E22, E23]. The bear's concern over margin contraction ignores the company's elite capital efficiency, where an ROCE of 29.96% to 71.5% and an ROE of 52.3% massively outperform the sector benchmarks of 6.66% and 5.13% [E7, E8, E9, E10, E49]. Furthermore, the company is entirely debt-free at Rs 0.00 Cr in borrowings down from Rs 0.17 Cr, rendering minor margin fluctuations negligible against a pristine balance sheet [E25, E36]. Finally, the reverse DCF indicates that today's market price of Rs 68.2 at a 10.6x P/E implies a negative earnings growth of -0.7%, proving that the stock is deeply mispriced relative to its 3-year compounded profit growth of 102% [E1, E3, E13, E32].

The bull’s reliance on absolute cash flow figures [E22, E23] ignores the alarming reality that the company is failing to convert its reported profits into actual cash, as evidenced by a poor cash conversion ratio of 0.23x [E21]. While the bull highlights elite capital efficiency, it fails to address that the company’s operating margin is trending downward [E18] and remains inconsistent on both a yearly and quarterly basis [E19, E20]. Conceded: [E25, E36]. Although the balance sheet is debt-free, the bull glosses over the significant operational risk signaled by the increase in debtor days from 40.2 to 56.8 [E39], which directly explains the disconnect between reported profits and cash generation [E21]. Furthermore, the bull’s reliance on a reverse DCF [E32] to suggest mispricing ignores the fact that the company provides zero dividend yield to shareholders [E4, E38], meaning investors are locked into a business that retains all earnings while struggling with deteriorating collection cycles [E39]. Finally, the bull’s focus on historical growth [E13] fails to account for the fact that the company’s operating margin has already begun to contract compared to three years ago [E18].
